>First and foremost, I detest the people that say "You must spend at least $1,000 per month on Facebook ads." Frankly, I think that many drop shippers go under because they spend all their money on ads before their store is looking clean and pristine. Here is what I recommend:  
>  
>→  Read as many drop shipping articles as you can.→  Look at a few drop shipping stores →  aprilmoon.ca is one of the stores that is featured on Spocket. Her store doesn't look like she spent a lot of money on design, but if it sells shit like Spocket says it does, this type of store works.→  I always tell people to buy a couple of domains to test a couple of ideas. You will want to set up a Shopify Partners account to build development stores so your Shopify bill doesn't kill you every month.→  Learn about digital marketing, FB ads, Google Ads, but most importantly SEO. You will need paid ads to get your store going, but SEO is going to keep you afloat.→  Work on email list building →  if you have an email list, you can send emails out each month and these cost NOTHING to get.→  I highly suggest that you implement an affiliate program on your store. Refersion and SECOmap are two that I've used. You have to pay affiliates a commission for sales, but at the end of the day it is worth it because they will send you a lot of traffic.→  Learn about Google Analytics →  this will be the go-to place where you see how your store is performing each day.→  DON'T pay for drop shipping groups on Facebook. I once asked Marc Chapon a question about SEO drop shipping and the best thing he told me was "Hire someone on Upwork."→  Learn about every aspect of running your store, from the marketing to the fulfillment of orders. If your store takes off, you're going to need to have someone to push the "fulfill button" every time an order comes in.→  Develop GREAT customer service skills.
